project.title: Differences in phosphorus and nitrogen cycling functions from periphyton associated with Chara spp. and Typha spp. in stormwater treatment areas of the Everglades
project.description: Everglades Stormwater Treatment Areas (STAs) were constructed to reduce total phosphorus (TP) to the Everglades Protection Area. Organic phosphorus (P) here is broken down by microbes, with this enzyme activity influenced by nitrogen (N) concentrations. Periphyton (microbial film growing on aquatic macrophytes and microbial mats) is important for the cycling of P and N and these functions may differ between periphyton associated with submerged aquatic vegetation (SAV) and emergent aquatic vegetation (EAV). To address this, periphyton sampling, surface water nutrient measurements, and phosphatase activity measurements were collected across wet and dry seasons from STA-2 Cell 4 at two different sites representing mid-flow (D112) and outflow (D139) areas. Microscopy and metagenomics were used to characterize the periphyton communities associated with Chara spp. (SAV) and Typha spp. (EAV). Collectively, the genomic information from both SAV and EAV demonstrates the functional capacity and diversity needed for growth in low TP environment of the STAs.
